newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH ELECTION - The key constituencies.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH ELECTION - The key constituencies.

text.p: Results of Sunday's final round of the parliamentary election in key constituencies.
-- Socialist leader LIONEL JOSPIN elected in the Haute-Garonne with 63.38 percent against 36.62 percent for UDF candidate Marie-Denise Xerri.
-- Outgoing prime minister and Bordeaux mayor ALAIN JUPPE elected in the Gironde, with 53.99 percent against Socialist candidate Gilles Savary (46.01 percent).
-- ALAIN LAMASSOURE, outgoing budget minister and government spokesman, loses seat in the Altantic Pyrenees with 49.27 percent against 50.73 percent for Socialist Nicole Pery.
-- Former Socialist prime minister LAURENT FABIUS re-elected in the Seine-Maritime with 72.91 percent against National Front candidate Guillaume de Tarle who polled 27.08 percent.
-- Former conservative president VALERY GISCARD D'ESTAING re-elected in Puy-de-Dome with 53.80 percent against Greens' Danielle Auroi (46.19 percent).
-- RPR Employment Minister ANNE-MARIE COUDERC loses in Paris, polling 44.98 percent, to Socialist Jean-Marie Le Guen (55.02 percent)
-- Environment Minister CORINNE LEPAGE loses in Paris, polling 45.50 percent against Socialist Patrick Bloche who scored 54.50 percent.
-- Overseas territories minister JEAN-JACQUES DE PERETTI (RPR) lost in Dordogne with 43.72 percent to Socialist Germinal Peiro (56.27 percent).
-- Justice Minister Jacques Toubon, RPR, loses Paris seat to Socialist Serge Blisko (51.47 percent).
-- National Front general secretary BRUNO GOLLNISCH loses in the Rhone with 26.55 percent of the vote against Socialist candidate Martine David's 44.06 percent.
-- Former conservative prime minister EDOUARD BALLADUR re-elected in Paris with 65.22 percent, comfortably beating Socialist Anne Le Moal (34.78 percent).
-- ROBERT HUE, Communist party leader, elected in Val d'Oise, polling 57.05 percent against RPR's Georges Monthron's 42.94 percent.
-- Socialist DOMINIQUE STRAUSS-KAHN, tipped as the next finance minister, elected in Val d'Oise with 59.65 percent.
-- Controversial Gaullist Paris mayor JEAN TIBERI re-elected in central Paris with 53.53 percent against Socialist candidate Lyne Cohen-Solal (46.47 percent).
-- Urban Affairs Minister ERIC RAOULT loses in the Seine-Saint-Denis, polling 40.47 percent. Socialist Alain Calmat won with 43.97 percent
-- National Front deputy leader BRUNO MEGRET loses in Bouches-du-Rhone (45.89 percent) against Socialist Henri Attilio (54.11 percent).
-- Socialist party spokesman FRANCOIS HOLLANDE wins in Correze with 54.22 percent, ousting Raymond-Max Aubert, a junior minister in Alain Juppe's first 1995 government.
-- Greens party spokeswoman DOMINIQUE VOYNET gains seat in Dole, eastern France, with 55.95 percent of the votes, beating UDF incumbent Gilbert Barbier (44.05 percent).
-- Former National Assembly leader PHILIPPE SEGUIN, tipped for prime minister if the right had won, re-elected in Vosges on 55.64 percent against socialist Gerard Weltzer (43.56 percent).
-- FRANCOIS LEOTARD, head of the centrist UDF alliance, re-elected in the Var with 62.71 percent, beating off the National Front's Jean-Pierre Risgalla.
-- Greens spokesman GUY HASCOET elected in Nord constituency with 46.74 percent, beating RPR's Michel Ghysel (33.88 percent).
-- Ecologist NOEL MAMERE elected in the Gironde with 60.01 percent against Gaullist Jean-Claude Barran (30.09 percent).
-- 1980s conservative security minister ROBERT PANDRAUD re-elected in Seine-Saint-Denis with 44.70 percent.
-- MARIE CAROLINE LE PEN, daughter of National Front leader Jean-Marie Lepen, loses in the Yvelines, polling 24.09 percent, to Socialist candidate Annette Peulvast-Bergeal (40.28 percent).
-- Socialist Strasbourg mayor CATHERINE TRAUTMANN elected in Lower Rhine on 50.15 percent against the UDF's 49.84 percent.
-- National Front mayor of Toulon JEAN-MARIE LE CHEVALLIER elected with 53.17 percent against Socialist Odette Casanova.
-- Former Socialist labour minister MARTINE AUBRY elected in Nord, scoring 60.81 percent against Gaullist RPR Jacques Donnay.
-- RPR general secretary JEAN-FRANCOIS MANCEL loses in Oise, (39.21 percent) to Socialist Beatrice Marre's 42.54 percent.
-- JACQUES BOMPARD, National Front mayor of Orange, loses three-way race in Vaucluse, polling 25.36 percent. RPR candidate Thierry Mariani won on 38.86 percent.
-- Farm Minister PHILIPPE VASSEUR (UDF) elected in the Pas-de-Calais on 53.43 percent against Socialist Jean-Claude Leroy (46.57 percent).
-- JEAN-LOUIS DEBRE (RPR), interior minister in the outgoing government, elected in the Eure with 53.65 percent, beating Radical Socialist Anne Mansouret (46.34 percent).
-- Former Socialist European affairs minister ELISABETH GUIGOU wins three-way race in the Vaucluse with 41.96 percent.
-- Socialist JEAN-MARIE BOCKEL wins Haut-Rhin with 41.66 percent, against 31.94 percent for centre-right Joseph Klifa and 26.40 percent for the National Front's Gerard Freulet.
-- Socialist HENRI EMMANUELLI re-elected in Landes on 60.93 percent, against 39.07 percent for Pierre Dufourcq (UDF).
-- Education minister FRANCOIS BAYROU (UDF) narrowly re-elected in the Atlantic Pyrenees on 50.92 percent, beating 49.08 percent for Socialist candidate Georges Labazee.
-- Former Socialist culture minister JACK LANG elected in Loir-et-Cher on 53.18 percent, beating UDF candidate Jacqueline Gourault (46.81 percent).
-- Anti-Maastricht rightist PHILIPPE DE VILLIERS wins comfortably in the western Vendee, taking 68.34 percent against 31.65 percent for Greens candidate Philippe Boursier.
-- PIERRE MOSCOVICI, co-author of the Socialist economic manifesto, wins in Doubs with 58.15 percent, against 41.85 percent for the outgoing RPR deputy Jean Geney.
-- Free-marketeering former finance minister ALAIN MADELIN (UDF) re-elected in Ille-et-Vilaine with 55.14 percent, beating Socialist candidate Simone Bourges (44.85 percent).

-- Leftist former defence minister JEAN-PIERRE CHEVENEMENT re-elected in Belfort with 55.3 percent, in a three-way run-off against Jacques Bichet of the centrist UDF (26.03 percent) and National Front candidate Michel Algrin (18.65 percent).
-- Former Socialist minister SEGOLENE ROYAL re-elected in Deux-Sevres constituency with 61.81 percent of the vote against 38.18 percent for Moreau Leopold of the centrist UDF.
